chapter: Paris, the Blackbirds and Noble Sissle
title: Tommy Ladnier in Sissle's band; Elmer Edwards in Wooding's
summary: Briggs says Ladnier was the one exception to the band's corny reputation, and recalls meeting him in Vienna and the trumpeter Elmer Edwards with Sam Wooding.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: We just had one exception, that
Well, he got, Ladnier to play, what, jazz solos, or something.
I just take a chorus on that. Just take a chorus. Ambitious, very, very southern.
Well, Ladnier was a nice guy. He was a heavy drinker, though.
Yes, yes, he was a nice boy. I really got along nicely when I first met him in Vienna. We got along nicely.
I forgot to say something about when I met Sam Wooding's band in Vienna. I was surprised. One of the trumpet players was -- did I mention that?
One of the trumpet players was also a member of the 15th, the present band that I was in, the New York 15th. His name was Elmer Edwards.
Yeh. He was a trumpet player and naturally we met in Berlin. He was with Sam Wooding's orchestra, we really had a ball.
I didn't drink, but I drank. And, -- where are we at now?
